items.q: Are habits reflexes, and how common are they?
items.a: Habits are **learned neuroplasticity**, not hard-wired reflexes. Up to **~70% of waking behavior** is habitual. Formation timelines vary (**Lally 2010: 18–254 days**).

items.q: What metric predicts whether a habit will stick?
items.a: **Limbic friction** — how hard the habit feels against anxiety or fatigue. Habit strength = **context dependence + limbic friction**; aim for **automaticity** you can move across times of day.

items.q: What should you do before executing a new habit?
items.a: **Procedural-memory visualization**: mentally walk the full step sequence once. Pair with **task-bracketing** — mark the start/stop envelope, not only the hard middle.

items.q: When should high-friction habits go on your calendar?
items.a: **Phase 1 (0–8 h after wake)** for habits you dread; Phase 2 for mellow ones; Phase 3 for sleep consolidation. **State beats clock** — rigid hour-of-day scheduling fails long-term.

items.q: How does the 21-day habit system work?
items.a: Target **6 habits/day for 21 days**, expect **4–5**; never compensate slips with doubles. Next 21 days **test automaticity** before adding more.

items.q: Which habits should you install first?
items.a: **Linchpin habits you actually enjoy** — only liked anchors reliably cascade into harder behaviors.

items.q: How do you break an unwanted habit effectively?
items.a: Use **positive cargo**: immediately after the unwanted behavior, do an easy replacement. Pre-behavior awareness alone rarely works; post-hoc replacement drives **synaptic depression** over time.

items.q: What does this Essentials cut omit?
items.a: **Dopamine spotlighting** (reward-prediction error across the habit envelope) is not covered here — see the full Huberman habits episode for that tool.
